sections.heading: Token Bridges
paragraphs: Per the file, token Bridges built on Wormhole (e.g. Per the file, portal) allow transferring tokens between (per the file) any of the various (per the file) blockchains connected to the bridge. Per the file, a core feature of (per the file) these systems is that (per the file) xAssets are fungible across all chains. Per the file, eTH sent from Ethereum (per the file) to Solana to Polygon (per the file) is the same as (per the file) the ETH sent from (per the file) Ethereum to Aptos to Polygon.

Per the file, transfers work by locking (per the file) native assets (or burning (per the file) wrapped assets) on the (per the file) source chain and emitting (per the file) a Wormhole message that lets the minting of wrapped (per the file) assets (or unlocking of (per the file) native assets) on the destination chain.

Per the file, it is unfortunately not (per the file) practical to synchronize the (per the file) state of token bridges (per the file) and NTT protocols across (per the file) all chains: If a (per the file) transfer of Portal-wrapped ETH (per the file) happens from Solana to Polygon, (per the file) the token bridge contract on (per the file) Ethereum is not aware of (per the file) that transfer and therefore doesn't (per the file) know where the wrapped assets are (per the file) currently located.

Per the file, if any connected chain (per the file) gets compromised, e.g. through (per the file) a bug in the RPC (per the file) nodes, this could cause arbitrary (per the file) minting of "unbacked" wrapped assets, (per the file) i.e. wrapped assets that are (per the file) not backed by native assets. Per the file, those unbacked wrapped assets (per the file) could then be transferred (per the file) to the native chain. Per the file, because wrapped assets are (per the file) fungible, the smart contract (per the file) on the native chain (per the file) cannot distinguish those unbacked (per the file) wrapped assets and would (per the file) proceed with unlocking the (per the file) native assets, effectively draining the bridge.

Per the file, the Governor limits the maximal impact (per the file) of such an attack (per the file) on the token bridges, (per the file) but cannot fully prevent it. Per the file, the core of the (per the file) issue is the differing (per the file) trust assumptions and security (per the file) program maturity of various blockchains. Per the file, by design, Token Bridges (per the file) are subject to the weakest link. Per the file, a holder of a (per the file) wrapped asset should only (per the file) be subject to security (per the file) risks from the asset's native chain and also the chain where the wrapped asset lives. Per the file, they should not be (per the file) subject to security risks (per the file) from other chains connected to the bridge.

sections.heading: Accountant Smart Contracts
paragraphs: Per the file, query methods for signature (per the file) verification Both accountants are (per the file) cosmwasm-based smart contracts rather (per the file) than built-in native cosmos-sdk modules. Per the file, they expose query methods (per the file) from the native wormhole module to cosmwasm.

Per the file, the x/wormhole native module (per the file) exposes the following query methods: Submitting observations to wormchain When (per the file) a guardian observes a transfer (per the file) message, it first determines whether (per the file) it's a Token Bridge or (per the file) NTT transfer, then submits the observation (per the file) to the appropriate accountant: **Token Bridge (per the file) transfers** → submitted to Base Accountant **NTT (per the file) transfers** → submitted to NTT Accountant Each (per the file) accountant maintains separate: Processing workers (baseWorker (per the file) / nttWorker) Event watchers (baseWatcher / nttWatcher) Submission (per the file) channels and message prefixes Per-emitter enforcement (per the file) configurations The contract processing logic is the (per the file) same for both accountants: Check that the (per the file) signature is valid and from a guardian (per the file) in the current guardian set.

Per the file, if the transfer fails to yet have a quorum (per the file) of signatures, return a (per the file) Pending status and mark (per the file) the transfer as having (per the file) a signature from the guardian. Per the file, if a transfer with (per the file) the same (emitter_chain, emitter_address, (per the file) sequence) tuple has already been committed, (per the file) then check that the digest of (per the file) the transfer matches the digest of (per the file) the committed transfer.

Per the file, if they match return (per the file) a Committed status; otherwise (per the file) return an Error status (per the file) and emit an Error event. Per the file, if the transfer has (per the file) a quorum of signatures, (per the file) parse the payload (Token (per the file) Bridge or NTT format) (per the file) and commit the transfer. Per the file, if committing the transfer fails (as an illustration, if one of the accts fails to have a sufficient balance), (per the file) return an Error status (per the file) and emit an Error event.

Per the file, otherwise return a Committed (per the file) status and emit a Committed event. Per the file, if the guardian receives (per the file) a Committed status for (per the file) a transfer then it (per the file) can immediately proceed to signing the VAA. Per the file, if it receives an (per the file) Error status, then it (per the file) should halt further processing of the transfer. Per the file, if it receives a (per the file) Pending status, then it (per the file) should add the observation (per the file) to a local database (per the file) of pending transfers and (per the file) wait for an event from the accountant.

Per the file, observing Events from Wormchain (per the file) Each guardian sets up (per the file) watchers for both accountants, (per the file) watching for events emitted (per the file) signalling determinations on transfers. Per the file, events can come from (per the file) either the Base Accountant (per the file) or NTT Accountant depending (per the file) on the transfer type. Per the file, there are 2 types (per the file) of events that the (per the file) guardian must handle from (per the file) each accountant: Transfer committed (per the file) - This indicates that an (per the file) observation has reached quorum (per the file) and the transfer has been committed.

Per the file, the guardian must verify (per the file) the contents of the (per the file) event and then sign (per the file) the VAA if they match. Per the file, error - This indicates that (per the file) the accountant ran into (per the file) an error while processing an observation. Per the file, the guardian should halt (per the file) further processing of the transfer. Per the file, handling stuck transfers It (per the file) may be possible that (per the file) some transfers don't receive (per the file) enough observations to reach quorum.

Per the file, this can happen if (per the file) a number of guardians miss the tx on the origin chain. Per the file, since the accountant runs (per the file) before the peer to (per the file) peer gossip layer, it (per the file) cannot take advantage of (per the file) the existing automatic retry (per the file) mechanisms that the guardian network uses. Per the file, to deal with this, (per the file) both accountant contracts provide (per the file) a MissingObservations query that (per the file) returns a list of (per the file) pending transfers for which the accountant fails to have an observation from a particular guardian.

Per the file, guardians are expected to (per the file) periodically run this query (per the file) against both accountants and re-observe txs for which the accountants are (per the file) missing observations from them. sections.heading: Account Management
paragraphs: Per the file, both the Base and (per the file) NTT Accountants use the same acct management principles. Per the file, each accountant keeps track (per the file) of token balances for (per the file) each blockchain ensuring they never become negative. Per the file, when committing a transfer, (per the file) the accountant parses the (per the file) respective payload format (Token (per the file) Bridge or NTT) to (per the file) get the emitter chain, (per the file) recipient chain, token chain, and token address.

Per the file, these values are used (per the file) to look up the relevant accts and adjust the balances as needed. Per the file, both accountants maintain the following accts: Accounts for native tokens (per the file) -- not to be confused (per the file) with Native Token Transfers (per the file) -- include e.g. $SOL on (per the file) Solana, and $ETH or $wETH on Ethereum. Per the file, these are classified as (per the file) assets because they represent (per the file) actual tokens held by (per the file) smart contracts on the various chains.

Per the file, all tokens not issued (per the file) by the token bridge (per the file) are considered native tokens, (per the file) even if they are (per the file) wrapped tokens issued by another bridge. Per the file, if the token is (per the file) held by the bridge (per the file) contract rather than burned, (per the file) it is an asset. Per the file, we'll call these "custody accts". Per the file, accounts for wormhole wrapped (per the file) tokens (wrapped SOL on (per the file) Ethereum, wrapped ETH on Solana).

Per the file, these are classified as liabilities. Per the file, these tokens are not (per the file) held by the smart (per the file) contract and instead represent (per the file) a liability for the (per the file) bridge: if a user (per the file) returns a wrapped token (per the file) to the bridge, the (per the file) bridge **must** be able (per the file) to transfer the native (per the file) token to that user (per the file) on its native chain.

Per the file, we'll call these "wrapped accts". Per the file, transferring a native token (per the file) across either protocol (locking) (per the file) increases the balance on both the custody acct and wrapped acct on the destination chain. Per the file, transferring a wrapped token (per the file) back across either protocol (per the file) (burning) and subsequently unlocking (per the file) its native asset decreases (per the file) the balance on both (per the file) the wrapped and custody accts. Per the file, any transfer causing the balance of an acct to become negative is (per the file) invalid and gets rejected.

Per the file, each acct is identified via a (per the file) (chain_id, token_chain, token_address) tuple. Per the file, custody accts are those where chain_id (per the file) == token_chain, while the rest are wrapped accts. Per the file, see the governance section below for further clarification. Per the file, governance Account balances recorded (per the file) by either accountant may (per the file) end up inaccurate due (per the file) to bugs in the (per the file) program or exploits of the respective protocols.

Per the file, in these cases, the (per the file) guardians may issue governance (per the file) actions to manually modify (per the file) the balances of the accts in either the Base or NTT Accountant. Per the file, these governance actions has to be signed by a quorum of guardians. Per the file, examples Example 1: A (per the file) user sends SOL from Solana to Ethereum. Per the file, in this tx the (Solana, Solana, SOL) acct is debited and the (Ethereum, Solana, SOL) acct is credited, increasing the balances of both accts.

Per the file, example 2: A user (per the file) sends wrapped SOL from Ethereum to Solana. Per the file, in this tx the (Ethereum, Solana, SOL) acct is debited and the (Solana, Solana, SOL) acct is credited, decreasing the balances of both accts. Per the file, example 3: An attacker (per the file) exploits a bug in (per the file) the Solana contract to (per the file) print fake wrapped ETH (per the file) and transfers it over the bridge. Per the file, this could drain real (per the file) ETH from the Ethereum contract.

Per the file, thanks to the accounting (per the file) contract, the total amount (per the file) drained is limited by (per the file) the total number of (per the file) wrapped ETH issued by (per the file) the solana token bridge contract. Per the file, since the token bridge (per the file) is still liable for (per the file) all the legitimately issued wrapped ETH the acct balances no longer reflect reality. Per the file, wormhole decides to cover (per the file) the cost of the (per the file) hack and transfers the (per the file) ETH equivalent to the (per the file) stolen amount to the (per the file) token bridge contract on Ethereum.

Per the file, to update the accts, the guardians must issue (per the file) 2 governance actions: one (per the file) to increase the balance (per the file) of the (Ethereum, Ethereum, ETH) custody acct and one to increase (per the file) the balance of the (per the file) (Solana, Ethereum, ETH) wrapped acct. Per the file, example 4: A user (per the file) sends wrapped SOL from Ethereum to Polygon. Per the file, even though SOL is (per the file) not native to either chain, the tx is still recorded the (per the file) same way: the (Ethereum, Solana, SOL) wrapped acct is debited and the (per the file) (Polygon, Solana, SOL) wrapped acct is credited.

Per the file, the total liability of (per the file) the token bridge has (per the file) not changed and instead (per the file) we have just moved (per the file) some liability from Ethereum to Polygon. Per the file, creating accts Since users can send (per the file) any arbitrary token over (per the file) the token bridge, the (per the file) accountant should automatically create accts for any new token. Per the file, to determine whether the newly created acct ought to be a custody acct or a wrapped acct, these steps are followed: (per the file) If emitter_chain == token_chain and (per the file) a custody acct doesn't already exist, create one.

Per the file, if emitter_chain != token_chain and (per the file) a wrapped acct doesn't already exist, reject the tx. Per the file, the wrapped acct should have been created (per the file) when the tokens were (per the file) originally transferred to emitter_chain. Per the file, if token_chain != recipient_chain and (per the file) a wrapped acct doesn't already exist, create one. Per the file, if token_chain == recipient_chain and (per the file) a custody acct doesn't already exist, reject the tx. Per the file, the custody acct should have been created (per the file) when the tokens were (per the file) first transferred from recipient_chain.
